method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; a seat-neutral core (poa-core.l4, with four regulative rules), date helpers (poa-dates.l4, built-in date functions, no daydate import, no YMD), the claimant's seat (poa-seat.l4) and the attorney's seat (poa-seat-attorney.l4), which restate no rule; exported questions take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Powers of Attorney Act 1998 (act-1998-022), the version in force from 2026-04-28 (current on 2026-11-06), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1998-022.txt (unofficial HTML conversion). Applied by ss 61D(6) and 107(4) and worked by hand: Succession Act 1981 ss 41(8) and 44(2)-(3), from ../../../succession-act-1981/registers/source-bundle/act-1981-069.txt. Not deposited and asked as facts: the Trusts Act 2025 (authorised investments); the Acts Interpretation Act 1954 (period counting: encoder's readings); the value of a penalty unit.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run poa-dates.l4 ; l4 run poa-core.l4 ; l4 run poa-seat.l4 ; l4 run poa-seat-attorney.l4 ; l4 run poa-cases-claimant.l4 ; l4 run poa-cases-attorney.l4
checks.result: 190 assertions written, 190 satisfied (155 claimant, 35 attorney), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-11-07); 4 #TRACEs with an expect line, each ending in the expected breach
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Claims about an attorney's dealings: s 33 (when power is exercisable); schedule 3 capacity and s 41(1); ss 113-114 (invalidity declarations); ss 96, 98, 99(2)-(3) (invalid powers, attorney and third-party protection); s 73 with s 118(2)-(4) (conflict transactions); s 87 (presumption of undue influence); ss 83-84, 86, 88-89 (Part 3 for enduring powers of attorney); ss 26, 61, 66(1), 71, 74A, 86(1) (maximum penalties); ss 66(2), 106 (compensation and account of profits, payee, 6-month times); s 107 with Succession Act s 41(8) (lost benefit, cap, 9 months); ss 61A-61D (a will beneficiary's interest in proceeds, 6 months, Supreme Court only); Succession Act s 44(2)-(3) as applied (the personal representative's distribution); ss 109A, 110 (standing and forum); s 122 (accounts and audit); ss 123-125 (dismissal, reasons, costs); ss 72, 82, 97, 105 (attorney's resignation, court advice, relief). Out: ss 1-6D, chapter 2 (other than s 26), chapter 3 parts 1-5 other than ss 33, 41(1), 61-61D, chapter 4, ss 67, 69-70, 74, 77-81, 85, 99(1), 100-104, 108-109, 111-112, 115-118(1), 120-121, ss 159-180, schedules 1-2.
seat: the claimant: the principal whose attorney dealt with their affairs, or, after the principal's death, the principal's personal representative, a beneficiary of the estate, or a person whose benefit in the estate was lost
seats: the claimant: the principal whose attorney dealt with their affairs, or, after the principal's death, the principal's personal representative, a beneficiary of the estate, or a person whose benefit in the estate was lost
the attorney answering a claim (an attorney under a general power of attorney, an enduring power of attorney, an advance health directive or another power of attorney, or a statutory health attorney)
